title: Elastic kernel switching for latency tiering
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This note collects design ideas, heuristics, and implementation notes for an elastic kernel switching mechanism in the serving runtime. Goal: at request dispatch time choose the most cost/latency-appropriate CUDA kernel for attention and KV work (FlashAttention-style fused kernels, fallback tiled kernels, and lightweight dequant/decompress paths for paged KV) to meet per-route latency SLO tiers without blowing GPU utilization or memory budgets.

Motivation / problem statement:
- We serve mixed workloads: short-chat-style (seq len 32–128, many concurrent requests) and long-completion / context-append (seq len 1–8 tokens per step but large prefix KV). Different kernels dominate cost/latency in different regimes.
- A single always-on kernel (e.g., optimized FlashAttention for long sequences) can be suboptimal for tiny batched requests or when KV pages are compressed and require on-the-fly dequant.
- Need a runtime policy that: (a) keeps p95/p99 SLOs for latency-sensitive routes, (b) maximizes throughput for cost-sensitive routes, and (c) degrades gracefully when paged-KV I/O or memory pressure occur.

Design overview (high-level):
1) Kernel catalog: annotate each kernel variant with an attribute vector.
   - KA: FlashAttention-v2-fused (best bandwidth for medium+ seq, high shared mem, high register pressure).
   - KB: small-batch-tiling (low-launch-overhead tiled matmul, good for seq<=64, batch>8).
   - KC: streaming-attn (reduced working memory, lower peak memory, slightly higher compute latency).
   - KD: quantized-kv-decode (fast path that consumes 4-bit/8-bit KV pages and emits float16/fp32 activations on-stream).
   - KE: naive fallback (safety, single-threaded per-request CPU fallback for correctness).

Each kernel row includes: preferred sequence length range, efficient batch size range, expected per-token latency at several batch/seq points (empirical microbench), GPU memory working set estimate, required shared mem, occupancy hint. Catalog stored as JSON metadata and kept next to kernel .so artifacts.

2) Decision function (runtime):
Input signals at enqueue time: route_id, prioritized SLO (p50/p95 target), input_seq_len, curr_batch_size for coalesced requests, route_priority (latency-sensitive vs throughput), KV-hit ratio (recent metric), estimated KV page read latency (if paged), model-quant-profile (whether KV is stored quantized), current GPU util and queue backlog.
Decision steps: 
   a) If route_priority == latency-sensitive and current_queue_backlog is low: prefer kernel with minimal cold-launch overhead (KB for tiny batches) unless seq_len > KB.max_seq.
   b) If route is throughput-oriented and batch_size >= KB.min_batch_for_efficiency: prefer KA (FlashAttention) when seq_len in its sweet spot.
   c) If paged-KV read latency > threshold or KV pages are compressed and not in memory: prefer KC (streaming) or schedule an early prefetch for KD followed by KA once pages arrive.
   d) If model uses quantized KV and KD exists, pick KD + KA combo: KD to decode into a transient buffer (pinned GPU memory allocator) then KA executed on decoded buffer.
   e) If GPU occupancy low but many small requests queued: attempt to coalesce requests into micro-batches and pick KB/KA depending on aggregated seq distribution.

Heuristics and thresholds:
- Microbench-derived breakpoints (example numbers, do not copy into perf claims without rerun):
   * FlashAttention (KA): best for seq >= 96 and batch>=4 — per-token latency ~0.22ms/token at seq=256,B=8 (A100-like).
   * Small-tile kernel (KB): wins for seq <=64 and batch <=16 — per-token ~0.08ms/token at seq=32,B=12.
   * Streaming (KC): similar to KA at very large prefix lengths where memory pressure causes paging; overhead amortizes for seq>512.
- KV-read threshold: if average KV page read (SSD-backed) > 2.5ms, mark request "KV-high-latency" and choose streaming path or prewarm prefetch.
- Launch overhead threshold: if expected compute < 400us, pick KB (lower overhead).

KV interaction patterns (paged KV concerns):
- Two access models: synchronous on-demand page fault (blocking) vs async prefetch pipeline. Kernel switching must be KV-aware because choosing KA without decoded KV means a stall.
- Proposed model: two-phase run for quantized/packed KV:
   1) scheduling stage: if KV in GPU cache -> regular path. If KV in host or compressed -> schedule KD decode kernel into a dedicated decode stream (stream-D). Post event, submit compute kernel into compute-stream (stream-C) that waits on event.
   2) opportunistic decode caching: decoded pages kept in ephemeral LRU keyed by (model,version,page-id,quant-profile). Eviction policy accounts for predicted reuse from recent request traces.

Implementation notes (CUDA specifics):
- Use one stream per request-group (latency-sensitive groups get high-priority CUDA stream via per-GPU priority levels). Decodes run on lower priority streams except when route is p99-sensitive.
- Use cudaEvent to coordinate decode->compute dependency instead of CPU blocking. This keeps the host thread free for scheduling.
- For kernels with very low compute time (microkernel KB), avoid dynamic parallelism and prefer a single-stream submission to reduce launch overhead.
- Implement a small thread-cooperative launch helper: when we coalesce N tiny requests, build a strided input tensor and call a batched tile-kernel with optimized lane usage to reduce per-request overhead.
- Memory allocation: pre-reserve a pool for transient decoded KV pages (pinned GPU memory) to avoid costly cudaMalloc on the hot path. Pool size adjustable by policy.

Observability / metrics to collect (minimum):
- chosen_kernel_id, seq_len, batch_size, route_id, decision_reason (enum), predicted_latency, actual_latency, kv_page_hit, kv_page_read_ms, decode_time_ms, queue_wait_ms, gpu_util, launch_overhead_us.
- Add tracing tags for kernel-switch decisions to tie regressions back to microbench artifacts in PRs.

Safety and fallback modes:
- If decode kernel KD fails or returns CRC mismatch, mark pages as corrupted -> fallback to CPU-deserialize path and route request to degraded throughput tier. Emit incident markers.
- If queuing latency exceeds SLO window and queued requests continue to miss, automatically lower the priority of throughput routes and force small-tile kernels for small inputs to protect latency-sensitive paths.

Rollout plan and experiments:
- Phase 0 (canary): implement decision function with decision logging only; route a small fraction (1–2%) of internal traffic and compare predicted vs actual latencies.
- Phase 1: enable adaptive policy for non-critical routes (status=throughput) and measure cost/unit improvements.
- Phase 2: enable latency-protected switching for selected real customer routes after manual review.

Microbench harness notes:
- Build microbench to sweep (seq_len: 8..2048, batch: 1..32, kv_on_gpu true/false, kv_quant 4/8/16). Produce a matrix of per-token and per-request latency and memory usage. Store outputs in a canonical CSV with header matching kernel catalog attributes.
- Include input noise to emulate host scheduling jitter.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to co-design prefetcher with wear-leveling of ephemeral decoded KV cache? Should decoded pages be shared across multiple models that use the same tokenizer/context?
- Can we get a cheap hardware timestamp for per-kernel compute time to refine launch-overhead heuristics more precisely than our host timers?
- Investigate whether an unsupervised learner (lightweight decision tree) can approximate the decision function better than hand-tuned thresholds.
- Add a safety parameter to force "single-kernel" mode for debugging and accurate A/B comparison.

Appendix: short pseudocode for runtime decision (simplified)

function pick_kernel(request):
  sig = (seq_len=request.seq, batch=request.batch, route=request.route)
  if request.route.priority == "latency" and queue_len < 4:
    if seq_len <= KB.max_seq and expected_compute < LAUNCH_THRESHOLD:
      return KB, "low-launch-overhead"
    if kv_page_read_ms > KV_HIGH_LATENCY:
      return KC, "kv-streaming"
  if batch >= KA.min_batch and seq_len >= KA.min_seq:
    return KA, "throughput-sweetspot"
  if request.model.kv_quant and KD.available:
    return KD_then_KA, "quantized-kv-fast-path"
  return KB_or_fallback, "default-tiling"
Notes about correctness: ensure kernels are validated on bit-exactness for critical model families before enabling on customer traffic. Add non-regression evals that run a deterministic set of prompts across kernels and diff logits/outputs.

End of note.
